story.en: Wednesday at LinkedIn's Organizational Development team. The VP of People is analyzing the company hierarchy to understand reporting structures, identify high-performing teams, and plan succession strategies. She needs to extract insights from performance reviews using text analysis, trace employee reporting lines from individual contributors up to the CEO, calculate department performance metrics, and identify key talent gaps. Using recursive CTEs to traverse the organizational hierarchy and string functions to analyze review comments, she can build a comprehensive organizational chart with performance insights.

Recursive CTEs use pannumbodhu organizational hierarchy traverse panna matrum string functions use pannumbodhu review comments analyze panna, comprehensive organizational chart build panna mudiyum performance insights-oda.

question.en: Build an organizational hierarchy showing each employee's name, department, direct manager, full reporting path from employee to CEO, department performance rating (average of employee ratings), and key skills extracted from performance comments. Extract skills using text patterns (e.g., 'sales', 'technical', 'leadership', 'management'). Show reporting chain depth and identify top performers per department.

title.en: Extract skills from performance review comments using pattern matching
title.ta: Performance review comments-nindha pattern matching use pannumbodhu skills extract pannu
title.hi: Performance review comments se pattern matching use karke skills extract karo
title.te: Performance review comments nundi pattern matching use chesi skills extract cheyyandi

steps.sql:
WITH skill_extraction AS (
  SELECT pr.emp_id,
         pr.comments,
         pr.rating,
         CASE
           WHEN LOWER(pr.comments) REGEXP 'sales|client|rapport' THEN 'Sales'
           ELSE NULL
         END AS skill1,
         CASE
           WHEN LOWER(pr.comments) REGEXP 'technical|expertise|problem-solving|coding' THEN 'Technical'
           ELSE NULL
         END AS skill2,
         CASE
           WHEN LOWER(pr.comments) REGEXP 'leadership|mentor|manager|coordination' THEN 'Leadership'
           ELSE NULL
         END AS skill3,
         CASE
           WHEN LOWER(pr.comments) REGEXP 'quality|consistent|reliable|excellence' THEN 'Quality Focus'
           ELSE NULL
         END AS skill4
  FROM performance_reviews pr
)
SELECT emp_id,
       CONCAT_WS(', ', 
                 NULLIF(skill1, NULL),
                 NULLIF(skill2, NULL),
                 NULLIF(skill3, NULL),
                 NULLIF(skill4, NULL)) AS extracted_skills,
       rating
FROM skill_extraction
WHERE extracted_skills IS NOT NULL;

en: String pattern matching using REGEXP identifies key skills mentioned in review comments.
LOWER() converts comments to lowercase for case-insensitive pattern matching.
Multiple CASE WHEN statements check for different skill keywords using regex patterns. The pipe symbol (|) acts as OR operator in regex.
CONCAT_WS() (Concatenate With Separator) joins non-null skill values with commas, automatically handling NULL values.
NULLIF() compares a value with NULL - if skill is not found, it returns NULL; otherwise returns the skill name.
This step extracts structured skill data from unstructured text comments for further analysis.
The WHERE clause filters results to show only employees with detected skills.
ta: String pattern matching REGEXP use pannumbodhu key skills identify pannuthandu review comments-la mention pannina.
LOWER() comments-a lowercase-aa convert pannuthandu case-insensitive pattern matching-kum.
Multiple CASE WHEN statements different skill keywords check pannuthandu regex patterns use pannumbodhu. Pipe symbol (|) regex-la OR operator-aaka work pannuthandu.
CONCAT_WS() non-null skill values join pannuthandu commas-oda, NULL values automatic-aaka handle pannuthandu.
NULLIF() value-a NULL-oda compare pannuthandu - skill find illa-na NULL return pannuthandu; illa skill name return pannuthandu.
Indha step unstructured text comments-nindha structured skill data extract pannuthandu further analysis-kum.
WHERE clause results filter pannuthandu detected skills irukkura employees mattum show panna.
hi: String pattern matching REGEXP use karke key skills identify hote hain jo review comments mein mention ho rahe hain.
LOWER() comments ko lowercase mein convert karta hai case-insensitive pattern matching ke liye.
Multiple CASE WHEN statements different skill keywords check karte hain regex patterns use karke. Pipe symbol (|) regex mein OR operator ka kaam karta hai.
CONCAT_WS() non-null skill values ko commas se join karta hai, NULL values ko automatically handle karte hue.
NULLIF() value ko NULL se compare karta hai - agar skill nahi mila toh NULL return hota hai; otherwise skill name return hota hai.
Ye step unstructured text comments se structured skill data extract karta hai further analysis ke liye.
WHERE clause results ko filter karta hai taaki sirf employees jinke paas detected skills hain vo dikhen.

title.en: Build recursive organizational hierarchy with reporting path
title.ta: Recursive organizational hierarchy build pannu reporting path-oda
title.hi: Recursive organizational hierarchy build karo reporting path ke saath
title.te: Recursive organizational hierarchy build cheyyandi reporting path tho

steps.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE org_hierarchy AS (
  -- Base case: Start with CEO
  SELECT e.emp_id,
         e.emp_name,
         e.department,
         e.manager_id,
         1 AS depth,
         CAST(e.emp_name AS CHAR(500)) AS reporting_path
  FROM employees e
  WHERE e.manager_id IS NULL
  
  UNION ALL
  
  -- Recursive case: Join with manager to build path
  SELECT e.emp_id,
         e.emp_name,
         e.department,
         e.manager_id,
         oh.depth + 1 AS depth,
         CONCAT(oh.reporting_path, ' -> ', e.emp_name) AS reporting_path
  FROM employees e
  JOIN org_hierarchy oh ON e.manager_id = oh.emp_id
)
SELECT emp_id,
       emp_name,
       department,
       manager_id,
       depth,
       reporting_path
FROM org_hierarchy
ORDER BY depth, emp_id;

en: Recursive CTEs are powerful for hierarchical data. They have two parts: a base case and a recursive case.
The base case selects the root employee (CEO) where manager_id IS NULL. This is the starting point of the recursion.
depth is initialized to 1 for the CEO, and reporting_path starts with just the CEO's name.
CAST(e.emp_name AS CHAR(500)) converts the name to a fixed-length character string for path building.
The recursive case uses UNION ALL to combine results and adds one level to the hierarchy.
It joins employees with the previous level using JOIN org_hierarchy, where the employee's manager_id matches org_hierarchy.emp_id.
depth increments by 1 for each recursion level, tracking how deep we are in the hierarchy.
CONCAT builds the reporting path by appending each employee name with ' -> ' separator.
ORDER BY depth ensures the results are displayed level by level, from CEO down.
ta: Recursive CTEs hierarchical data-kum powerful. Base case matrum recursive case nu rendu parts irukku.
Base case root employee (CEO) select pannuthandu manager_id IS NULL. Recursion-oda starting point indha.
depth 1-aa initialize aagum CEO-kum, matrum reporting_path CEO-oda name mattum start aagum.
CAST() name-a fixed-length character string-aaka convert pannuthandu path building-kum.
Recursive case UNION ALL use panni results combine panni hierarchy-ku oru level add pannuthandu.
Employee-ia join pannuthandu previous level-oda employee's manager_id match pannumbodhu org_hierarchy.emp_id-oda.
depth increment aagum 1 recursion level-kum, hierarchy-la depth track panna.
CONCAT reporting path build pannuthandu employee name append panni ' -> ' separator-oda.
ORDER BY depth results display pannuthandu level by level, CEO-nindha down-kum.

title.en: Combine hierarchy with performance metrics and skills
title.ta: Hierarchy-a performance metrics matrum skills-oda combine pannu
title.hi: Hierarchy ko performance metrics aur skills ke saath combine karo
title.te: Hierarchy ni performance metrics mariyu skills tho combine cheyyandi

steps.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE org_hierarchy AS (
  SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, e.manager_id, 1 AS depth,
         CAST(e.emp_name AS CHAR(500)) AS reporting_path
  FROM employees e
  WHERE e.manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, e.manager_id, oh.depth + 1,
         CONCAT(oh.reporting_path, ' -> ', e.emp_name)
  FROM employees e
  JOIN org_hierarchy oh ON e.manager_id = oh.emp_id
),
skill_extraction AS (
  SELECT pr.emp_id,
         ROUND(AVG(pr.rating), 2) AS avg_rating,
         GROUP_CONCAT(CASE
           WHEN LOWER(pr.comments) REGEXP 'sales|client|rapport' THEN 'Sales'
           WHEN LOWER(pr.comments) REGEXP 'technical|expertise|problem-solving' THEN 'Technical'
           WHEN LOWER(pr.comments) REGEXP 'leadership|mentor|coordination' THEN 'Leadership'
           WHEN LOWER(pr.comments) REGEXP 'quality|consistent|reliable' THEN 'Quality'
           ELSE NULL
         END, ', ') AS key_skills
  FROM performance_reviews pr
  GROUP BY pr.emp_id
),
dept_performance AS (
  SELECT oh.department,
         ROUND(AVG(se.avg_rating), 2) AS dept_avg_rating
  FROM org_hierarchy oh
  LEFT JOIN skill_extraction se ON oh.emp_id = se.emp_id
  GROUP BY oh.department
)
SELECT oh.emp_id,
       oh.emp_name,
       oh.department,
       oh.depth,
       oh.reporting_path,
       COALESCE(se.avg_rating, 0) AS employee_rating,
       COALESCE(se.key_skills, 'No skills recorded') AS key_skills,
       COALESCE(dp.dept_avg_rating, 0) AS dept_performance,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(se.avg_rating, 0) > COALESCE(dp.dept_avg_rating, 0) THEN 'Top Performer'
            WHEN COALESCE(se.avg_rating, 0) >= COALESCE(dp.dept_avg_rating, 0) - 0.5 THEN 'Solid Performer'
            ELSE 'Developing'
       END AS performance_tier
FROM org_hierarchy oh
LEFT JOIN skill_extraction se ON oh.emp_id = se.emp_id
LEFT JOIN dept_performance dp ON oh.department = dp.department
ORDER BY oh.department, oh.depth, oh.emp_name;
